## Telework related questions

### 2025 New work from home question (`work_from_home`)

**Does each person ever work from home?**

- No
- Yes, some of the time (less than 50% of the time)
- Yes, most of the time (at least 50% but less than 100% of the time)
- Yes, all of the time (100% of the time)

:::{.callout-note}
#### Logic

- *if household has 1 or more members who worked for pay/profit or were on leave last week*
- *if household has 1 member or more ‘on leave': For any household member on leave (e.g., parental leave, medical leave), please respond based on their work arrangements prior to leave.*
- Programmer: Show list of persons age 16+ with paid_work = “yes” or “on leave”

:::
   
### telework frequency (`telecommute_freq`)

**Currently, how many days <do you/does name> typically work from home or telework (instead of going to work that day)?**

- 6-7 days a week
- 5 days a week
- 4 days a week
- 3 days a week
- 2 days a week
- 1 day a week
- 1-3 days a month
- Less than monthly
- Never *hide if job_type is work ONLY from home or remotely (telework, self-employed)*

:::{.callout-note}
#### Logic

- Programmer: if (paid_work is “yes” or “on leave”) AND work_from_home is NOT “all of the time”

:::

## Teleworker and Telework Status Definitions

:::{.callout-important}
Data universe for this analysis: full/part time or self-employed workers
:::

The following analysis has two ways of identifying teleworkers and telework status:

1. **Teleworkers** are the workers who telecommute more than one day per week or work fully at home
2. **Telework status** assignments
   - **Fully At Home**: workers working from home all of the time
   - **Hybrid**: workers working from home some or most (not all) of the time and telecommuting at least 1 day/week
   - **Fully In Person**: workers telecommuting less than 1 day/week


## Telework trend

- Roughly two-thirds of workers worked fully in person outside of home in 2023 and 2025.
- Those who work fully at home peaked in 2021 at about one-third.
- Hybrid workers made up about one-quarter of all workers from 2021 to 2025.

```{r}
#| label: fig-telework-trend
#| fig-cap: "Telework trend"
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 6

df_plot <- psrc_hts_stat(df_hts_data, "person", 
                         c("telecommute_status"),
                         # exclude NAs in calculation: only considering workers
                         incl_na=FALSE) %>%
  group_by(survey_year) %>%
  mutate(
    prop_position = case_when(telecommute_status=="Fully At Home"~0,
                              telecommute_status=="Hybrid"~.data$prop[1],
                              telecommute_status=="Fully In Person"~sum(.data$prop[c(1,2)]))
  )

ggplot(df_plot, 
       aes(x=factor(survey_year), y=prop, fill=fct_rev(telecommute_status))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(y= prop_position, label=scales::percent(prop, accuracy = 1),
                color=telecommute_status),
            vjust = -0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0,1), color = "#cbcbcb", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = psrc_fill_segment$telecommute_status)+
  scale_color_manual(values = psrc_font_segment$telecommute_status, guide = "none")+
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  psrc_style() +
  theme(axis.title = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_blank())
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-telework-trend

df_plot %>%
  select(-c("prop_position")) %>%
  # function sourced from Analysis/util.R
  get_table_format()
```

## Commute mode share

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
Sample sizes were low for commuting with other modes in 2021
:::

- Most workers who travel outside of home for work drove.
- Workers who took transit decreased significantly in 2021 and stayed around 7\% to 9\% (differences are within margins of error) since.
- Active Modes (incl. walk, bike and micromobility) is consistently at 4\% to 6\% (differences are within margins of error)


```{r}

stat_telework_status <- function(group_var){
  
  res <- psrc_hts_stat(df_hts_data, "person", 
                       c(group_var,"telecommute_status"),
                       incl_na=FALSE) %>%
    filter(telecommute_status %in% c("Fully At Home","Hybrid"),
           .[[group_var]] !="Prefer not to answer")

  return(res)

}

stat_teleworker <- function(group_var){
  
  res <- psrc_hts_stat(df_hts_data, "person", 
                       c(group_var,"telecommute_freq_1plus"),
                       incl_na=FALSE) %>%
    filter(telecommute_freq_1plus == "telecommute at least 1 day/week",
           .[[group_var]] != "Prefer not to answer")

  return(res)
}

plot_teleworker <- function(group_var, type="both", 
                               color_year=psrc_colors$pgnobgy_10,
                               color_cat=psrc_colors$blues_dec){
  
  res <- stat_teleworker(group_var)
  
  if( type %in% c("year","both") ){
    
    # print your charts
    print(
      ggplot(res, 
             aes(x=telecommute_freq_1plus, y=prop, fill=!!sym(group_var))) +
        geom_col(position = position_dodge(),width = 0.95) +
        geom_text(aes(label=scales::percent(prop, accuracy = 1)),
                      position = position_dodge(0.95),
                  vjust = -0.3, 
                  size = 10, size.unit="pt") +
        errorbar_switch(geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = prop - prop_moe, ymax = prop + prop_moe),
                                      position = position_dodge(0.95),
                                      width = 0.1), 
                        on=params$errorbar) +
        facet_wrap(~ survey_year, ncol=7)+
        geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#cbcbcb", linewidth = 0.3) +
        scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = color_year)+
        psrc_style() +
        theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
              legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
              axis.title = element_blank(),
              axis.text.x = element_blank(),
              axis.text.y = element_blank())
      )
  }
  
  if( type %in% c("cat","both") ){
    
    print(
      ggplot(res, 
             aes(x=factor(survey_year), y=prop, fill=factor(survey_year))) +
        geom_col(width = 0.8) +
        geom_text(aes(label=scales::percent(prop, accuracy = 1)),
                  vjust = -0.3, 
                  size = 10.5, size.unit="pt") +
        errorbar_switch(geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = prop - prop_moe, ymax = prop + prop_moe),
                                      width = 0.1), 
                        on=params$errorbar) +
        facet_wrap(as.formula(paste("~", group_var)), ncol=7)+
        geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#cbcbcb", linewidth = 0.3) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = color_cat)+
        scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
        psrc_style() +
        theme(legend.position = "none",
              strip.text = element_text(size = 11),
              panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
              panel.spacing.x = unit(0.5, "lines"),
              axis.title = element_blank(),
              axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10.5),
              axis.text.y = element_blank())
    )    
    
  }
  
}

tbl_teleworker <- function(group_var){
  
  # result table with formatting
  stat_teleworker(group_var) %>%
    select(all_of(c("survey_year",group_var,"telecommute_freq_1plus","count","prop","prop_moe","est","est_moe"))) %>%
    # function sourced from Analysis/util.R
    get_table_format()
  
}
```

## Telework by demographic characteristics


### Household income

- Strong positive correlation between income and working from home

```{r}
#| label: fig-telework-income
#| fig-cap: "Teleworker by household income"
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 6

plot_teleworker("income_50_100","year")
```

- The share of teleworkers for households with income under $50,000 were not affected by the pandemic
- The share of teleworkers for households earning \$50,000 or more increased significantly in 2021 during the pandemic. Since the pandemic, The share for households earning \$50,000 to \$99,999 dropped to almost pre-pandemic levels while the share for households earning \$100,000 or more are still more than 40\%.

#### Telework status by household income

```{r}
#| label: fig-telework-status-income
#| fig-cap: "Household income: Telework status by year"
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-width: 7
#| warning: false

plot_telework_status <- function(group_var){
  
  df <- stat_telework_status(group_var)
  
  # get error bars for combined
  df_plot_errorbar <- stat_teleworker(group_var) %>%
    mutate(ymin = prop-prop_moe,
           ymax = prop+prop_moe) %>%
    select(all_of(c("survey_year",group_var,"ymin","ymax")))
  
  # get stat for "Fully At Home" and "Hybrid" combined 
  df_total <- df %>%
    mutate(telecommute_status="( %): Hybrid & Fully At Home") %>%
    summarise(prop_label = paste0("(",scales::percent(sum(prop), accuracy = 1),")"),
              prop = 0,
              .by = c("survey_year",group_var,"telecommute_status"))   %>%
    # merge with error bars
    left_join(df_plot_errorbar, by = c("survey_year",group_var))

  df_plot <-  df %>%
    # create text label for df
    mutate(prop_label = scales::percent(prop, accuracy = 1)) %>%
    # merge with combined
    bind_rows(df_total) %>%
    mutate(telecommute_status = factor(telecommute_status, 
                                       levels=c("Fully At Home","Hybrid","( %): Hybrid & Fully At Home"))) %>%
    # calculate text label position
    mutate(
      prop_position = case_when(telecommute_status=="Fully At Home"~.data$prop[1],
                                telecommute_status=="Hybrid"~sum(.data$prop[1:2]),
                                telecommute_status=="( %): Hybrid & Fully At Home"~sum(.data$prop[1:2])+0.04),
      .by = c("survey_year",group_var)
    )
  
  print(
    ggplot(df_plot, 
           aes(x=factor(survey_year), y=prop, fill=fct_rev(telecommute_status))) +
      geom_col(width = 0.85) +
      geom_text(aes(y= prop_position, label=prop_label,
                    color=telecommute_status),
                vjust = 1.1) +
      errorbar_switch(geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
                                    width = 0.1), 
                      on=params$errorbar) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#cbcbcb", linewidth = 0.3) +
      facet_wrap(as.formula(paste("~", group_var)), ncol=7) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c("white","#00A7A0","#8CC63E"))+
      scale_color_manual(values = c("#4C4C4C","#4C4C4C","#4C4C4C"), guide = "none")+
      scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
      psrc_style() +
      theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 11),
            axis.title = element_blank(),
            panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
            axis.text.y = element_blank())
  )
}

plot_telework_status("income_50_100")
```

## Travel behaviors

### Workweek trips by telework status

- Fully in person workers make fewer "Social/Recreation/Meal" non-mandatory trips

```{r}
#| label: fig-telework-triprate
#| fig-cap: "Workweek trips by telework"
#| fig-asp: 0.4
#| fig-width: 10


# number of people by telecommute status
df_telecommute_status <- psrc_hts_stat(df_hts_data, "person",
                                       c("telecommute_status"),
                                       # exclude NAs in calculation: only considering workers
                                       incl_na=FALSE) %>%
  filter(survey_year == 2025) %>%
  rename(n_person = est) %>%
  select(telecommute_status, n_person)

# trip rate by person
res <- psrc_hts_stat(df_hts_data, "trip", 
                     c("telecommute_status", "dest_purpose_rate"),
                     # exclude NAs in calculation: only considering workers
                     incl_na=FALSE) %>%
  filter(survey_year == 2025) %>%
  rename(n_trip = est) %>%
  select(telecommute_status, dest_purpose_rate, n_trip) %>%
  left_join(df_telecommute_status, by = "telecommute_status") %>%
  mutate(trip_rate = n_trip /n_person) %>%
  arrange(dest_purpose_rate) %>%
  group_by(telecommute_status) %>%
  mutate(
    trip_rate_position = case_when(dest_purpose_rate=="Errands/Shopping/School/Other"~.data$trip_rate[1],
                                   dest_purpose_rate=="Social/Recreation/Meal"~sum(.data$trip_rate[c(1,2)]),
                                   dest_purpose_rate=="Work"~sum(.data$trip_rate[c(1,2,3)]))
  )

ggplot(res, 
       aes(x=telecommute_status, y=trip_rate, fill=fct_rev(dest_purpose_rate))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(y= trip_rate_position, label=scales::number(trip_rate, accuracy = 0.1),
                color=dest_purpose_rate),
            hjust = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#cbcbcb", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#F05A28","#00A7A0","#8CC63E"))+
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#4C4C4C","#4C4C4C","#4C4C4C"), guide = "none")+
  coord_flip()+
  psrc_style() +
  theme(axis.title = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```


```{r}
#| label: tbl-telework-triprate
res %>%
  mutate(trip_rate = scales::number(trip_rate, accuracy=0.01)) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols="telecommute_status", names_from="dest_purpose_rate", values_from="trip_rate") %>%
  knitr::kable()
```
